provider.name: The Reptile Database
provider.organization_type: global reptile taxonomy, nomenclature, synonymy, classification, distribution, bibliography, image, checklist, download, and reference infrastructure
provider.description: The Reptile Database is a global taxonomic reference for living reptiles, providing accepted names, synonyms, classification, authorship, type information, distributions, common names, references, images, checklists, statistics, and update histories.
institutional_context: Museums, universities, herpetological societies, taxonomists, and photographers
External biodiversity, conservation, nomenclatural, and bibliographic infrastructures

purpose.summary: Crawl-ready source catalog for Reptile Database documentation, taxonomy, nomenclature, synonyms, classification, distributions, checklists, references, images, machine interfaces, downloads, validation, licenses, citations, software, standards, and related authorities.
purpose.authoritative_notice: The Reptile Database, its editors and taxonomic specialists, original taxonomic literature, official nomenclatural registries, museum type specimens, official releases, and cited external sources remain authoritative.

notes: Verify whether a supported public API exists and identify canonical routes.
Verify authentication, methods, parameters, schemas, pagination, rate limits, and deprecations.
Do not infer undocumented editorial or administrative endpoints from browser traffic.
Do not store credentials, API keys, cookies, tokens, or session identifiers.
Capture exact Reptile Database, editor, contributor, image, download, API, and third-party legal wording.
Separate taxonomic facts, database compilation, bibliography, images, distributions, downloads, and software.
Preserve taxon IDs, accepted-name IDs, source references, citation, access date, release version, license URI, rights holder, and provenance.
Do not assume photographs, illustrations, publications, or third-party data share the same rights as taxonomic facts.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Website routes, search parameters, API availability, download formats, schemas, taxonomic coverage, and legal pages may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every species, subspecies, genus, image, reference, country checklist, API result, or download record when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store credentials, API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, private editorial notes, unpublished submissions, or session identifiers.
Taxonomic facts, bibliography, images, distribution data, API output, downloads, and software may carry different rights.

Always preserve taxon ID, accepted-name ID, scientific name, authorship, rank, parent, original combination, synonyms, taxonomic and nomenclatural status, type data, common names, distribution, references, images, external identifiers, release version, citation, rights, source URL, and provenance.
